about.title: A little about me
about.headline: From the first idea to a live application.
about.text: I'm João Vinicius. I build web and mobile applications and AI agents, working across interfaces, APIs, integrations and deployment.
about.text2: I started in IT support, where I began automating tasks with Python. As I took on more development work, I moved into full stack development while keeping hands-on experience with infrastructure and operations.

self_employed.description:
I work on the architecture, development and maintenance of two strategic AI solutions: a conversational agent for lead qualification and conversion, and a platform for analyzing and processing large volumes of legal documents.

I evaluate and benchmark large language models (LLMs), considering performance, response quality, latency and cost-effectiveness.

I develop and evolve scalable AWS architectures using AWS Lambda and Amazon ECS, focusing on performance, scalability and cost optimization.

I develop APIs and integrations in Python and TypeScript with FastAPI and NestJS, as well as solutions using RAG, embeddings, vector databases and semantic search.

fictor.role: Senior Full Stack Developer · Generative AI & AI Agents
fictor.description:
I led the architecture and development of the corporate Super-App, building mobile, web and backend applications with Flutter, React and NestJS to centralize services, operational processes and internal communication across the group.

I designed and developed a multitenant HR platform with RBAC using NestJS, TypeScript, Next.js and React. It covers job opening requests and approvals, candidate management through a Kanban pipeline and an integrated Candidate Portal for applications, tracking and synchronization.

I refactored the WhatsApp debt collection agent with FastAPI and LangGraph, integrating it with the Agrosys ERP through an MCP Server, with automated messages and human handoff.

I maintained the group's portals and analytics solutions, including Insights360 and Power BI Embedded, with Microsoft Entra ID, RLS and Azure DevOps integration.

I automated builds and deployments with CI/CD pipelines in Azure DevOps, Docker and Kubernetes.

atalaia_dev.description:
I designed and built a debt collection agent integrated with WhatsApp, automating negotiation steps and contributing to the recovery of outstanding payments.

I built Python data integrations and automations to collect, process and deliver information for corporate applications and business analysis.

I deployed Metabase, integrating data, building analytical models and creating dashboards to support business decisions.

I delivered internal systems for booking vehicles, accommodation and meeting rooms, with NestJS APIs and React and TypeScript interfaces.

atalaia_it.description:
I provided technical support, maintained IT infrastructure and supported corporate systems to help keep operations running.

I developed up to 20 RPA solutions with Python and Selenium to automate repetitive operational work and reduce manual tasks.

I contributed to the Atalaia Alimentos website in Django, including configuration and deployment on a GoDaddy VPS.

As my responsibilities expanded into software development and process automation, I was promoted internally to Full Stack Developer.

projects.title: Selected work

super_app.description: An internal app for Fictor Alimentos that brings together vehicle reservations, hotel bookings, announcements and dashboards. I built the mobile and web interfaces and backend, with corporate authentication and module-level permissions.
super_app.problem: Vehicle reservations lived in spreadsheets, announcements in emails and business metrics in separate portals. Hotel bookings were handled by phone.
super_app.solution: I built InCubo with Flutter, React and NestJS, integrating Azure AD login, module-level permissions, Firebase and RabbitMQ notifications, AI-assisted reservation validation and Power BI dashboards. It runs on Kubernetes with Azure DevOps deployment.
super_app.result: The app was adopted across the group and replaced four separate systems. The project reported around 40% fewer operational IT requests.
super_app.name: InCubo
super_app.image_alt: Internal announcements screen in the InCubo mobile app
super_app.summary: Bookings, announcements and business data in one app. I built the mobile app, web interface and backend connecting the group's operations.

fictor360_pbi.description: I integrated Power BI reports into the super-app. Each person sees the data allowed by their profile, using user and Azure AD group rules.
fictor360_pbi.problem: Individual license costs grew with the company. Restricting data by department required duplicate workspaces, making permissions harder to maintain.
fictor360_pbi.solution: I built a Power BI Embedded portal. The app checks Azure AD users and groups and injects row-level security roles into each session token. Dashboards and workspaces are managed through the API.
fictor360_pbi.result: Access moved from individual licensing to a capacity-based model. Reports became available inside the app with per-user data permissions.
fictor360_pbi.name: Fictor360
fictor360_pbi.image_alt: Fictor360 portal displaying Power BI reports
fictor360_pbi.summary: Power BI dashboards inside the app, with access defined by each person's profile.

hr_platform.description: A recruitment system with approval workflows, Kanban, deadline tracking and semantic résumé analysis using Azure OpenAI and pgvector.
hr_platform.problem: Hiring requests passed through forms, emails and spreadsheets. Approvals and deadlines were hard to track, and résumés arrived across scattered emails.
hr_platform.solution: I built approval flows for roles and hiring requests, RAG-based résumé matching and Teams interview integration. Azure AD handles authentication and permissions, Bull processes background jobs, and webhooks synchronize the candidate portal.
hr_platform.result: HR can track candidates and deadlines in a Kanban, with automatically scored résumés. Queued processing handles batches without blocking the interface.
hr_platform.name: People management
hr_platform.image_alt: Fictor Alimentos people management platform interface
hr_platform.summary: From opening a role to the interview: approvals, Kanban and résumé analysis in one HR platform.

fictor360_ai.description: An agent that takes natural language questions, generates DAX queries and accesses Power BI semantic models. Answers stream back alongside the queried data.
fictor360_ai.problem: For deeper analysis, managers depended on someone who knew DAX and the structure of their Power BI models.
fictor360_ai.solution: I connected the agent to Power BI through MCP, exposing tables, measures and relationships as context. The flow generates and validates DAX before execution. I used LangChain, LangGraph and Azure OpenAI, with WebSocket streaming and example question-query pairs to guide generation.
fictor360_ai.result: Users can ask a question and receive data with a chart without writing DAX. The conversation sits alongside the dashboard during analysis.
fictor360_ai.name: Fictor360 AI
fictor360_ai.image_alt: Fictor360 conversational agent alongside a dashboard
fictor360_ai.summary: Questions become Power BI queries, with answers and charts on the same screen.

candidate_portal.description: A public recruitment portal connected to the internal HR system, with Google, LinkedIn or email login, résumé analysis and webhook synchronization.
candidate_portal.problem: HR received résumés by email. Candidates had no place to follow their applications, and recruiters needed a way to publish open roles.
candidate_portal.solution: I built the portal in NestJS and React, separate from the internal system. I integrated OAuth2, scoring on résumé upload and HMAC-SHA256 signed webhooks. Privacy controls and per-IP rate limits protect sensitive endpoints.
candidate_portal.result: Candidates follow their applications through the portal. HR receives scored résumés directly in the management system.
candidate_portal.name: Candidate portal
candidate_portal.image_alt: Fictor Alimentos jobs and applications portal
candidate_portal.summary: A place to find roles, send a résumé and follow an application, connected to the HR system.

data_pipeline.description: Python pipelines for extracting, transforming and loading internal data. I deployed Metabase so managers could access their metrics, with dashboards and consolidation in Power BI.
data_pipeline.problem: ERP systems, spreadsheets and APIs supplied inconsistent formats. Consolidation was manual, and managers depended on IT to retrieve metrics.
data_pipeline.solution: I automated extraction and transformation with Python and Pandas, deployed Metabase and connected dashboards to Power BI for company reporting.
data_pipeline.result: More than ten automated dashboards run daily. Managers access their metrics without asking IT for each query.
data_pipeline.name: Data pipelines
data_pipeline.image_alt: Illustrative diagram of a Python data pipeline
data_pipeline.summary: ERP, spreadsheet and API data brought together with Python to power the company's reporting.

yt_signals.name: YT Signals
yt_signals.summary: YouTube comments organized by topic and sentiment in an interactive map with supporting evidence.
yt_signals.description: Uses AI to analyze YouTube comments and organize topics, sentiment and evidence in an interactive map, with a web application and a local Chrome extension.
yt_signals.problem: Understanding audience feedback requires reviewing scattered messages and manually connecting opinions, topics and examples.
yt_signals.solution: I integrated the YouTube Data API with OpenAI to structure comments into topics, sentiment and insights. I built the React interface, Node.js server and a Chrome extension that opens an analysis from a video, with local history and graph navigation.
yt_signals.result: A locally runnable web application and extension with a summary, map and comments supporting each topic. The extension has not been published in the store; public API access and usage limits are still evolving.
yt_signals.image_alt: YT Signals map showing topics, comments and a summary of a YouTube video analysis

agente_financeiro.name: Agente Financeiro
agente_financeiro.summary: Personal finance in Telegram using text, voice and documents, with calculations and writes handled by the server.
agente_financeiro.description: An agent for recording and querying personal finances in Telegram through text, voice, images and PDFs, with document review before entries are recorded. The project is undergoing validation.
agente_financeiro.problem: Recording expenses and tracking multiple wallets through messages requires interpreting requests while keeping calculations, authorization and balance changes outside the AI model.
agente_financeiro.solution: I built the agent in Python with FastAPI, PostgreSQL and model-invoked tools. The server validates authorization, calculates balances and controls writes; images and PDFs become proposals the user can review and confirm.
agente_financeiro.result: Implemented flows for income, expenses, transfers, scheduled entries, notifications and reviewable document imports. Local tests cover the financial rules; continuous operation with real services is still being validated.

theo_glpi.name: Theo GLPI
theo_glpi.summary: Conversational support that gathers context and prepares GLPI tickets for review and confirmation.
theo_glpi.description: A support agent that gathers context, prepares GLPI tickets and tracks updates in the conversation. Integration with the real Microsoft Teams environment is in development.
theo_glpi.problem: Support requests often lack the details needed to understand the issue, classify it and record a useful ticket for the technical team.
theo_glpi.solution: I built an agent using Node.js, OpenAI, the Microsoft Teams SDK and the GLPI API. It collects symptoms, suggests simple troubleshooting steps and presents a summary in Adaptive Cards. The server creates the ticket only after user confirmation.
theo_glpi.result: Diagnosis, classification, review, ticket creation, queries and notifications are implemented in the development environment. Deployment to real Teams, Microsoft authentication and linking Teams users to GLPI requesters remain pending.

filmoteca_tmdb.name: Filmoteca TMDB
filmoteca_tmdb.summary: Movie discovery, filtered search and local favorites in a native Android application.
filmoteca_tmdb.description: An Android application for discovering, searching, filtering and saving TMDB movies, with a paginated catalog and favorites available offline.
filmoteca_tmdb.problem: Exploring a movie catalog and maintaining a personal collection requires combining remote search, filters, pagination and access to favorites without a network connection.
filmoteca_tmdb.solution: I built the application in Kotlin, using Jetpack Compose for the main screens, an XML Fragment for details and the TMDB API through Retrofit and Paging 3. Favorites are stored locally with Room.
filmoteca_tmdb.result: An application with an editorial home screen, filtered search, movie details and a local collection of favorites. The current version requires no login and does not synchronize the collection with a TMDB account.
filmoteca_tmdb.image_alt: Filmoteca TMDB home screen with a featured movie and catalog carousels

ask_about_me.name: Ask About Me
ask_about_me.summary: A content and RAG backend that answers questions about my background with evidence and citations.
ask_about_me.description: A content and RAG backend that answers questions about my background using hybrid search and citations. Integration with the public portfolio chat is in development.
ask_about_me.problem: An assistant about my background needs to answer from published material and keep the content consistent with the evidence retrieved by search.
ask_about_me.solution: I built the backend in FastAPI with PostgreSQL and pgvector, vector and text retrieval, generation with validated citations and a bilingual publishing panel. Indexing prepares a candidate generation before replacing the active index.
ask_about_me.result: The RAG pipeline, content endpoints and bilingual publishing are available locally, with retrieval evaluation. Public integration with the portfolio is still in development; the current question demonstration continues to use prepared answers.

ask.q12: How do you evaluate and improve an AI agent?
ask.q12_chunk1: LLM evaluation and benchmarking based on performance, response quality, latency and cost-effectiveness.
ask.q12_chunk2: In the AWS agent, comparison of retrieval strategies and questions with and without answers in the context.
ask.q12_answer: I evaluate and compare LLMs based on performance, response quality, latency and cost-effectiveness. I also test questions with insufficient information to check when the agent should decline to answer. In the AWS RAG experiment, I compared search strategies, retrieval of the correct sources, rejection of unanswerable questions and latency. This work includes observability and reliability of AI systems.
ask.q13: What technical decision did you reconsider?
ask.q13_chunk1: In the AWS agent experiment, hybrid retrieval found more context but also accepted cases that should have been rejected.
ask.q13_chunk2: The recorded decision was to prioritize query rewriting and expansion and keep hybrid retrieval optional.
ask.q13_answer: In the AWS RAG experiment, hybrid retrieval found more sources but also accepted questions that had no answer in the context. That result led to choosing query rewriting and expansion as the default while keeping hybrid retrieval optional. The decision considered both what retrieval found and what it should reject.
